library. So okay, solution one, let's try to add some concurrency to this. Fix 2: prefetching

so we came up with solution two which was that we have a background thread that fills up a queue ahead of time and it's always stays ahead of the consumer which means that you your producer is producing examples at a multiplier of your tra of your consumer and so the trainer is never bottlenecked on actually requesting the data. When it requests data it's it is available on demand. There's a caveat to prefetching. It makes your model and data loader checkpointing and resumption like a little intricate of a process and it can also suffer from a cold start period in which your queue is actually getting filled up uh so it can be ready for training. Um but uh if you work around those those details I think pre-fetching is a is a great idea. Um yeah, so I think making sure your producer is always ahead of your consumer will be will pay great dividends for you here.

Um unsurprisingly, we achieved close to 0 seconds of data fetching and processing per batch because we've already fetched data and processed it way before the trainer even needs it. Um and so we've effectively solved both the data load and the transform bottlenecks. So after these two mitigations, we thought we were done. throughput up GPUs fed however we observe that the data

Fix 3: zero-copy with Ray's object store

transport costs still linger in fact they've gone up so every sample transfers a large amount of like image arrays across process boundaries multiple times every sample is pickled on the worker copied to the coordinator and then repickled onto the trainer per sample per step we have a mem copy that nobody really asked for so what h how this manifest is that your data generator can often oo. Um, and so multimodal tensors are huge. They're megabytes per sample. Um, and so by default, every sample is returned by value, which means this that these expensive arrays are copied over from process to process. So a fix for this, you can come up with an object store. Um, this is a nice convenience method of that array provides you. Each sample carries a object reference which is just a pointer to the data.

Um and then the driver just holds the pointer. The tensor never round trips to the head node. Um and the Megatron data parallel ranks they can just directly call the race store to fetch the data as they need. So with every choice of your parallelism and concurrency solution, you always have to think about the commu added communication costs. So plan wisely around that. Okay. Yeah. And we were able to eliminate an extraneous like put object uh kind of call that our prefetcher solution had that we did not have to deal with by using the ray store. And we can see that our communication costs go down and the ratio of the time spent waiting also

goes down. So to recap, we took a serial baseline. We added concurrency for data loading and processing. We added pre-fetching to stay ahead of training requests and we added the race store to minimize data transfer. We went from a baseline weight ratio of 85% to 20%. And you can see that the saw to uh pattern that you see in the top graph is alleviated uh to a large extent which means that our utilization of the GPUs has gone up. pipeline, let's try to scale it up to like a production run. While doing that, we observed that our weight time ratio for the same pipeline went up when all we did was scale some numbers. The network card bottleneck

what happens is that there's a bottleneck on the network interface card of that of that node. Uh which means that while we're packing all of this working and processing into specific nodes that their network throughput is not able to keep up with the demand of the training pipeline. Um so at this point we did a little bit of digging into the frameworks that we are using and we saw that by default Ray schedules workers on this it prefers to schedule workers on the same nodes and colllocate workers which means that it's easy to bottleneck one machine before you move to another machine. So what we did was consider a possibility where we disagregate this whole process where workers are spread across multiple nodes. Um so they can do their own image processing and storing and in a lazy just in time manner are retrieved and used by our DP rings.

second is a spread scheduling mechanism. Um neither of these actually helped in a small scale experiment but together they had um a synergistic effect in a large scale experiment. And so now this is the final pipeline that we've accomplished a concurrent eager um and a data access pattern aware system that shares the training across loads and enables that GAPU stay warm while providing smoothness and stability in training. set by the bottleneck. So these are the learnings we get from this talk if nothing else. Um GPUs are expensive but sometimes the biggest battles happen outside of the GPU. So first ask yourself are you CPU bound or GPU bound? Are you IO bound or computebound? And then solving one bottleneck often exposes another. Overall, profiling your baseline helps you move the needle. Um, yeah, thank you everyone for attending the talk. Uh, if you have any questions, I'm happy to answer them. Thanks.
aiSummary: 一位多模态训练工程师把 GPU 利用率低的问题追溯到串行取数，并展示并发、预取、Ray 对象引用和分散调度如何在训练扩容过程中不断转移瓶颈。
oneSentenceSummary: 一位多模态训练工程师把 GPU 利用率低的问题追溯到串行取数，并展示并发、预取、Ray 对象引用和分散调度如何在训练扩容过程中不断转移瓶颈。
summary: 演讲分析了一条类似 Qwen3-VL 的多模态监督微调流水线：图像获取与 CPU 预处理让昂贵的 GPU 长时间空闲。串行基线获取一个批次需超过 100 秒，模型计算约需 15 至 20 秒，GPU 利用率因此约为 15%。异步取图与 Ray actor 处理首先缩短等待，后台生产队列又在训练器请求前预取数据。但这暴露出另一项成本：大幅图像数组在多个进程之间反复拷贝。团队改用 Ray 对象引用，让数据并行进程直接取得数组，而无需绕经协调节点。演讲称，等待时间占比由约 85% 降至 20%。扩容后，集中在同一节点的 worker 又挤满网卡；分散调度与零拷贝检索配合，报告额外带来约 50% 的吞吐提升，尽管两项设置在小规模实验中都不明显。这是一段有具体时间与瓶颈演变的一手性能排查。标题中的 90% 利用率在开头被提到，但详细复盘主要支持等待比例变化，最终利用率的测量口径并不完整。

mainPoints.point: 优化模型内核前，先剖析完整训练流水线。
mainPoints.explanation: 基线中，一个批次的取数和准备超过 100 秒，模型工作只有约 15 至 20 秒，GPU 因而长期等待。

mainPoints.point: 并发和预取分别对应不同瓶颈。
mainPoints.explanation: 异步 IO 获取图像，Ray actor 处理 CPU 密集型变换，后台生产者提前填充队列，避免训练器请求时才开始准备。

mainPoints.point: 对象引用可减少大型多模态张量的反复传输。
mainPoints.explanation: 样本无须在 worker、协调器与训练器之间一再序列化；数据并行进程可以通过 Ray 对象存储直接取得数组。

mainPoints.point: 规模变化会改变调度决策的优劣。
mainPoints.explanation: 大规模数据并行时，worker 集中部署会挤满网卡；分散调度配合零拷贝才显现收益，而小规模测试未必看得出来。

keyQuotes: 关键是让解决办法对应真正的瓶颈。
每次选择并行或并发方案，都要考虑随之增加的通信成本。
我们的基线等待比例从 85% 降到了 20%。
剖析基线，才能找到真正推动性能的地方。
